hints.title: Reverse Aggregation View
hints.text: Instead of simulating divisions forward from one unit, think in reverse by merging completed tasks into combined units with additional division overhead.

hints.title: Smallest Pair Priority Selection
hints.text: Greedily combine the two smallest strain times. If two tasks finish earliest, pairing them creates the most balanced sub-tree.

hints.title: Repeated Heap Reduction
hints.text: Extract two smallest elements a and b, compute splitTime plus maximum of a and b, and insert the result back until one root element remains.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def minEliminationTime(self, timeReq: list[int], splitTime: int) -> int:
        heap = timeReq.copy()
        heapq.heapify(heap)
        while len(heap) > 1:
            a = heapq.heappop(heap)
            b = heapq.heappop(heap)
            merged = splitTime + max(a, b)
            heapq.heappush(heap, merged)
        return heap[0]
```

complexity.notes: Min-priority extraction merges smallest pairs in logarithmic steps.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Forward branching trees have exponential possible schedules.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A priority structure keeps task durations sorted during merges.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Model the reverse Huffman merge principle for parallel execution.
